evals.prompt: This FastAPI inventory module works, but make it simpler, more idiomatic, and easier to maintain without changing its API behavior.
evals.expected_output: Improve activates, inspects the real implementation and selected versions, makes only bounded evidence-backed quality improvements, preserves behavior, and verifies the changed surface.

evals.prompt: Use the improve skill to refactor this working module while preserving behavior.
evals.expected_output: Improve follows its preservation-first workflow and does not reopen product or architecture decisions.

evals.prompt: Users receive a 500 error when saving inventory. Find the cause and fix it.
evals.expected_output: Improve should not own the request; the failing behavior routes to debug/root-cause work.

evals.prompt: Improve this small module. It is already clear, current, idiomatic, has one responsibility, and matches accepted architecture.
evals.expected_output: Improve does not manufacture abstractions or churn. It reports that no meaningful bounded improvement is justified or makes only a concrete evidenced change if one exists.

evals.prompt: Refactor a straightforward FastAPI + SQLAlchemy Core use case. There is no concrete need for repositories, Unit of Work, CQRS, or mediator layers.
evals.expected_output: Improve keeps the simple project architecture and does not introduce named patterns or abstraction layers merely because they are common in templates.

evals.prompt: Improve code that uses a legacy lifecycle/configuration idiom on a selected current framework version.
evals.expected_output: Improve checks the actual selected version and current primary guidance, replaces genuinely legacy/deprecated usage when worthwhile, and avoids unrelated modernization.

evals.prompt: Improve this module, but the proposed cleanup would require changing the accepted database authority and service boundary.
evals.expected_output: Improve preserves the accepted architecture and routes the consequential redesign to architect instead of silently making it as a refactor.

evals.prompt: Improve this working query because it looks slow, but no latency/profile/query-plan evidence has been collected.
evals.expected_output: Improve does not perform speculative performance rewriting. If performance is the real goal, it composes performance-engineering and establishes a relevant baseline before changing the query.

evals.prompt: Improve a working component by simplifying duplicated state. The project has no coverage target and the behavior is best exercised through existing browser checks.
evals.expected_output: Improve verifies preserved behavior with the cheapest strong evidence and does not create mandatory unit tests, TDD steps, mocks, or coverage work merely because code changed.
